title: Reproducing the FRMF Risk Analysis Template on an Open Model

# Reproducing the FRMF Risk Analysis Template on an Open Model

**Problem:** The 'Frontier AI Risk Management Framework in Practice' technical report demonstrates a structured risk analysis on a frontier model, but the worked methodology has not been shown to be runnable by external parties on an accessible open-weight model, leaving its third-party usability untested.

**Direction:** Take the public FRMF risk-analysis structure (capability assessment, risk modeling, mitigation mapping) and execute a scoped version end-to-end on one open-weight model for a single risk domain (e.g., cyber-uplift), documenting every place where the template assumes internal access you don't have and how you substituted public evidence.

**Why it matters:** Whether risk-management frameworks can be exercised by outsiders determines if they enable real third-party assurance or only lab self-attestation. Single open model, public methodology, no proprietary data.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'Frontier AI Risk Management Framework in Practice: A Risk Analysis Technical Report' (arXiv:2602.14457, Feb 2026), testing external reproducibility of its risk-analysis workflow.

title: Which Dangerous-Capability Evaluations Actually Require External Model Access?

**Direction:** Compile a taxonomy of published dangerous-capability eval methods, code each by the minimum access tier required (public outputs, API, logits, weights, fine-tuning), and validate the coding by attempting the lowest-tier methods on an open model. title: Robustness of Open-Weight Bio Safeguards to Adversarial Fine-Tuning: A Governance-Costing Replication

original_idea.body:
# Robustness of Open-Weight Bio Safeguards to Adversarial Fine-Tuning: A Governance-Costing Replication

**Problem:** A recent paper shows open-weight genome language model safeguards can be stripped via adversarial fine-tuning, but governance discussions lack a clear sense of the COST (compute, data, expertise) needed to defeat such safeguards — which determines the real marginal risk.

**Direction:** Without touching dangerous biological content, replicate the structure of the finding on a benign proxy: take an open model with a refusal-style safeguard on an innocuous restricted topic, measure how little fine-tuning (steps, examples, GPU-hours) removes the safeguard, and translate this into a 'safeguard-durability cost curve' for governance.

**Why it matters:** Marginal-risk governance of open weights hinges on how cheaply safeguards fall; a public cost curve is exactly the diffuse, long-horizon evidence labs won't prioritize. Single GPU, small fine-tune, benign proxy domain.

**Relevant context:** Extends 'Open-weight genome language model safeguards: Assessing robustness via adversarial fine-tuning' (arXiv:2511.19299, Nov 2025), abstracting it to a benign safeguard-durability cost measurement.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: small fine-tune of an open model with a refusal safeguard, clear methodology, novice+mentor.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped experiment (cost-to-strip curve) but spans setup+measurement; well-defined success criterion.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected long-horizon public-good evidence on safeguard robustness labs won't prioritize; needs no internal access.

**Why it matters:** If the technical backbone of mandated disclosure fails under everyday use, the regulation is unenforceable; a clean survival-curve study is exactly the diffuse, public-good evidence regulators need. Open tools, CPU/light-GPU.
